content.title: About
content.content: Rice, cooked with milk is a ready‑to‑eat product obtained by boiling rice in milk. It has a soft, creamy texture, a mildly sweet flavor, and is often used in baby foods, desserts, and as a quick breakfast.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice with milk is a traditional dish in many Asian countries, especially Japan (okān) and India (kheer).
The combination improves the bioavailability of some B‑vitamins.
In Soviet cuisine, rice with milk was commonly served as a sweet porridge with sugar or honey.
When prepared correctly, the product retains most nutrients from both ingredients.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice carbohydrates are quickly digested, providing rapid energy.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Milk supplies calcium essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: Contains vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D in milk aids calcium absorption.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The smooth, creamy texture is easy on the stomach, especially for children and sensitive adults.

items.title: Provides protein
items.content: Combining plant protein from rice with milk protein offers a complete amino‑acid profile.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience bloating, gas, or diarrhea after consumption.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey requires complete avoidance of the product.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rice has a high GI, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Added sugar content
items.content: If sweetened, the product can raise blood sugar levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy rice with milk hot as a breakfast, add fruit, nuts, or honey. It can be used in desserts, casseroles, and as a base for baby meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions for up to 2 months. Check smell and texture before use.
